newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar futures slump below support.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar futures slump below support.

text.p: London's March white sugar contract slumped to below psychological support at $300 per tonne as the white's premium came under pressure from selling on the New York raw's market, traders said on Tuesday. Commission house and broker selling accounted for the bulk of the March volume, which was mainly composed of outright dealings, they said.
"It seems to be premium selling...New York has gone all the way down and the premium hasn't widened at all," said one. "There just seems to be a glut of selling there."

March closed down $7.00 at $297.70 and May closed down $6.40 at $298.00 after an intraday low of $297.00. Total volume was 4,096 lots. New York's equivalent March contract tumbled 43 points to an intraday low of 10.23 cents/lb before recovering to 10.29, down 37 cents off at the London close off a high of 10.69 cents.
March last dipped below $300.00 on November 22, when values slipped back inside a major downtrend channel in place since the middle of September.
The spot contract in Paris also lost ground, possibly on account of pre-hedging against Wednesday's European Union tender for sugar export licences.
March was down $7.10 at $297.50 and May down $6.10 at $298.50.
